name: statusline
description: A five-row Claude Code statusLine (session, model, context, quota, work) plus a per-subagent row renderer -- the only documented surface carrying live context-window pressure. Two scripts and one top-level settings key (`statusLine`), plus the `subagent-rows` mod, a project-local plugin under `.claude/skills/` that draws the agent panel's rows and replaces the deprecated `subagentStatusLine` key: no hook registrations, no verify step. Colors default to the terminal's own ANSI-16; an opt-in m3l-design truecolor palette is never applied unless the project sets it. Split from `harness-extras` so a project that already has its own status line can take that pack's hooks without a collision.
adoptNotes: The statusline scripts read only the stdin payload, .git/HEAD (via node:fs, never a git subprocess) and process.availableMemory()/os.totalmem(), so they install anywhere a .claude/ directory exists -- no dependency on the baseline's file layout. The one real adopt risk is the top-level `statusLine` key: a project that already defines it collides, and its existing value must be shown and decided on, never overwritten -- if it is set, skip that key and the two scripts that render it and install only the `subagent-rows` mod. A project that still carries the deprecated `subagentStatusLine` key keeps it untouched (the mod's row text overrides it); tell the owner the key is deprecated and can be removed, and never remove it without asking. A statusLine in .claude/settings.local.json (or one passed with --settings) also shadows the project one; the user's own ~/.claude/settings.json ranks lower and does not -- check those before concluding the pack is wired. rate_limits.spend_limit and prompt_cache need Claude Code v2.1.251+, and the `subagent-rows` mod needs Claude Code v2.1.326+ (the `AgentRow` render site) and a trusted project folder -- it loads as `subagent-rows@skills-dir`, is skipped under `-p` in an untrusted folder, and setting `subagent-rows@skills-dir` to `false` under `enabledPlugins` in `.claude/settings.local.json` turns it off; before v2.1.326 it never fires and rows keep Claude Code's default look. Each statusLine segment renders only when present, so an older Claude Code degrades to fewer segments rather than breaking. The scripts behave the same on macOS and Linux; the memory segment uses process.availableMemory() (Node 22+), and on macOS with an older Node it is hidden rather than shown from os.freemem(), which undercounts there. Below roughly 40 columns the layout drops segments by priority rather than wrapping. Colors are the terminal's ANSI-16 by default; `GROUNDWORK_STATUSLINE_THEME=m3l-design` in the `env` block of .claude/settings.json switches the status line to the m3l-design truecolor palette (light or dark from COLORFGBG), and NO_COLOR turns color off under either. The pack never sets that key: add it only when the owner explicitly asks, add-only, and if `env.GROUNDWORK_STATUSLINE_THEME` already holds another value show it and ask. The `subagent-rows` mod reads the same key through `$.settings.read({ key: "env" })` (it cannot see the shell's environment), so its first row after a start uses the default colors and later rows use the theme; it takes light or dark from Claude Code's `theme` setting (read the same way; `auto` and custom themes say nothing), then from COLORFGBG in that env block, then assumes dark. These scripts used to ship inside the `harness-extras` pack; a project that installed that pack before the split keeps its files untouched.
